subject: suppressing or renaming grouping columns from adply/ddply

messages.author: e531efa2753b204e
messages.subject: suppressing or renaming grouping columns from adply/ddply
parts:
Simple example:

a <- array(runif(100), c(10, 10))
adply(a, 1, function(x) c(mean=mean(x))) #two columns, "X1" and "mean,"

However, if the function returns something named "X1" it clobbers the indexing column.

adply(a, 1, function(x) c(X1=mean(x))) #only one column in result

ddply is also subject to this clobbering:

ma <- melt(a) #has columns "X1", "X2", and "value"
ddply(ma, "X1", with, mean(value)) # has columns "X1" and "V1"
ddply(ma, "X1", with, c(X1=mean(value))) # has column "X1" only

Now, "X1" isn't an unusual enough name that I can guarantee my data won't contain it, which means problems for me if i am trying to write a reasonably robust and generic function that uses aaply/ddply. Moreover, there are a lot of cases where I don't actually want the grouping columns.

What I'd like to be able to do is either suppress the output of the indexing column(s), or be able to specify what their names will be.

Is there a nice way to do that?

Peter

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: suppressing or renaming grouping columns from adply/ddply
parts:
Hi Peter,

You can name the array dimnames:

dimnames(a) <- list(Var1 = 1:10, Var2 = 1:10)

adply(a, 1, function(x) c(mean=mean(x)))
# Var1 mean
# 1 1 0.5568333
# 2 2 0.4218855
# ...

Hadley
